title: Claim
description: One sourced statement about a BIP. One file per claim at bips/<NNNN>/claims/<id>.yaml, so bot pull requests never conflict.

statement.description: The claim in BipWatch's own words. The quote is the proof, the statement is the reading.

area.description: For tasks, open questions and objections: the type of work, by who would pick it up. design: deciding how the protocol should work (open design decisions, alternatives, parameters); writing: editing the spec document itself (clarifications, warnings, missing sections, wording that changes meaning); engineering: code (reference implementation, node, wallet, library, server); testing: test vectors, tests, fuzzing; review: reading and checking a spec, a change or code; research: analysis, benchmarks, security arguments, data; ux: how users and wallets meet it (flows, formats, naming, design); coordination: agreement across projects or the ecosystem, outreach; activation: deployment of a consensus change (signaling, parameters, miner and node readiness).

part_of.description: For tasks, open questions and objections about work outside the BIP's own text that moves it forward: the companion BIP or project it belongs to, e.g. "BIP 375" or "light-client index". Absent when the item is about the BIP itself.

status.description: Lifecycle of tasks, objections and open questions: open (raised, not yet resolved as far as BipWatch knows), addressed (resolved, with the source showing it), disputed, unknown.

scope.description: Stances only: what the position is about. proposal: the BIP as a whole or its approach. change: one edit to the BIP's text, usually a bitcoin/bips pull request amending it. implementation: code that implements the BIP. An ACK of an amendment is review of that change, not support for the proposal.

change.description: For change- and implementation-scoped stances: the pull request or proposed change the stance is about, when it has a link.

subject.description: Who or what the claim is about: the implementer, or the person or org taking a stance.

state.description: shipped: in a release; merged: in the main branch, not in a release yet; partial: shipped with parts missing (e.g. send only); in-review: an open pull request; planned; proof-of-concept; not-supported.

scanning.description: How the implementation detects incoming payments, where relevant.

networks.description: Networks it runs on, when that is the point (e.g. a soft fork live only on signet).

applies_to_version.description: Spec version the claim was made against. Used to flag stale stances when the spec changes materially.

type.description: primary: the spec, the author, or the implementer. secondary: an aggregator or press.

revision.description: Git commit of the source when it is versioned (the spec, a repo file).

quote.description: Verbatim text from the source. Keep it short. Must match the source exactly.

verified.description: True once code has matched the quote against the archived source byte for byte.

extracted_by.description: human:<handle>, or model:<model-id> for LLM extraction.

reviewed_by.description: Handle of the person who approved it. null while the claim is pending review.
